Legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently gave a talk at the Startup School 2026 event, and the video of her talk has now been uploaded to Y Combinator's YouTube channel, which you can watch below.

Susan Kare shared many wonderful stories and design insights

More than 40 years have passed since the original Macintosh was launched, and the system's graphics, fonts, icons and overall UI elements are still eye-catching today, with no loss of their original charm.

In fact, many of the elements Susan Kare designed for the original Macintosh can still be found in macOS today, whether in spirit or preserved in their original form. From the Command key symbol, to the "Happy Mac" smiley face startup icon, to the system font, to the pointing hand cursor, Kare's work not only shaped the visual language of the Mac, but also influenced the entire personal computer industry.

Although anyone who has looked into Apple's history should have seen Kare's sketches, or even read or heard her mention these early works in interviews, every time you hear her share in person the passion that drove her and the frustrations of that era, it is always particularly interesting — because back then, graphical user interfaces and bitmap graphics were fields that almost no one had ventured into.

So, if you are interested in design, in Apple's history, or simply want to hear someone passionately share their favourite subject in the field they have devoted their life to mastering, Kare's talk is absolutely worth watching.

In addition to talking in detail about her work at Apple, Kare also shared how she came to join the company, showed her work after she left, shared many little stories from Apple's early days, and paired them with quotes from other legendary designers to give everyone an extra boost of encouragement.
